Definition: from the same as G4556; sardine (G3037 being implied), i.e. a gem, so called:--sardine.
BiblicalUsage: A sardine stone is what the King James Version calls the gem in the vision of the throne: he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone, with a rainbow round about the throne. The Greek text behind the King James Version reads the adjective form here, while the text I have checked reads the noun form of the same stone.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the stone matters more than the spelling: the throne is ringed with colour, and the King on it is beautiful to look upon.
